blocks.text: Who is God according to Christianity?
Christians believe there is one eternal God who created everything that exists.
God exists eternally as Father, Son and Holy Spirit — three Persons who share one divine nature.

blocks.title: In one sentence
blocks.text: God is the eternal, uncreated source of all that exists, who has revealed himself to humanity.
Belief in one eternal God runs through the entire arc of the Bible, from the opening lines of Genesis to the closing vision of Revelation.
This is not a belief that developed gradually out of polytheism, as some critics claim, but one the biblical authors present as revealed from the very beginning.
When Moses asked who was sending him to confront Pharaoh, God answered with a name that describes his very nature: pure, self-existent being.

blocks.commentary: God reveals his eternal, self-existent nature — he does not depend on anything else for his existence.

blocks.caption: God appears to Moses in the burning bush.

blocks.text: In the New Testament, Jesus applies this same divine name to himself — a claim his listeners understood clearly enough to try to stone him for it.

blocks.commentary: Jesus applies the divine name I AM directly to himself, claiming eternal existence before Abraham.
John identifies Jesus as the eternal Word who was with God, and was God, from the very beginning.

blocks.text: Everything that begins to exist has a cause. The universe began to exist. Therefore the universe has a cause — one that is itself uncaused, since an infinite chain of causes explains nothing on its own.

blocks.title: Natural theology
blocks.text: This argument does not rely on Scripture or revelation — it proceeds from reason and observation of the natural world alone.
Christian philosophers have long argued that this uncaused cause must be eternal, immaterial, and immensely powerful — attributes that align with the God described in Scripture.

blocks.note: The unmoved mover argument, later developed by Aquinas into the Five Ways.

blocks.text: Belief in this one eternal God, and in Christ's divinity, was affirmed consistently by the earliest Christian writers — not invented centuries later.

blocks.title: Who created God?
blocks.steelman: Many atheists argue that if everything requires a creator, then God must also require one.
blocks.response: Christianity does not claim that everything requires a cause — only things that begin to exist do. God, by definition, is eternal and never began to exist, so the question does not apply to him.

blocks.title: Isn't God just a human invention?
blocks.steelman: Some argue that belief in God evolved naturally as an explanation for what ancient people didn't understand.
blocks.response: The Christian claim doesn't rest on ignorance filling gaps in knowledge — it's supported independently by philosophical argument, the testimony of Scripture, and the historical case for Christ's resurrection.

blocks.title: Why doesn't God reveal himself more clearly?
blocks.steelman: If God wanted everyone to believe, he could simply appear and remove all doubt.
blocks.response: Christianity holds that God has revealed himself — through creation, through Scripture, and definitively through the person of Christ — while still preserving the freedom to accept or reject that revelation.

blocks.text: The Church teaches that while human reason can arrive at the existence of God, it is only through revelation that we come to know him as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

items: God is eternal — he has no beginning and no end.
God is one — there is only one God, not many.
God is the Creator of everything that exists.
God has revealed himself throughout history, culminating in Christ.
Jesus reveals the Father and shares in the same divine nature.

blocks.text: The Christian understanding of God as one eternal being in three Persons is supported by Scripture, historical testimony, philosophical reasoning, and the consistent teaching of the Church across two thousand years.

blocks.question: Can God change?
blocks.answer: No. Christian teaching holds that God's divine nature is immutable — he does not grow, learn, or change over time.

blocks.question: Is the Trinity three separate gods?
blocks.answer: No. Christians believe in one God who exists eternally as three distinct Persons — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — sharing a single divine nature.

blocks.question: Does the Old Testament teach the Trinity explicitly?
blocks.answer: Not explicitly, but Christians see it foreshadowed in passages describing the Word, Wisdom, and Spirit of God acting alongside him.
